saved_record.correction_summary: Removed furosemide because it was not necessary to the tested construct and created an avoidable second medication-management branch. Tightened the item to recognition and immediate management of suspected digoxin toxicity; added cardiac monitoring to the correct response; rebuilt distractors to remain within the same construct; verified the 3.1 mmol/L potassium value against Mayo Clinic Laboratories; expanded the exact DailyMed locator to §§2.5, 5.3, 10.1, and 10.2; changed difficulty from hard to moderate.
saved_record.educational_objective: Recognize suspected digoxin toxicity when gastrointestinal symptoms and ventricular ectopy occur in a client with hypokalemia, and respond by withholding digoxin, maintaining cardiac monitoring, and obtaining current digoxin, electrolyte, and renal-function data while escalating the finding.
saved_record.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Give the scheduled digoxin, continue cardiac monitoring, notify the provider of the low potassium, and recheck potassium later.","B":"Give digoxin with food, continue cardiac monitoring, notify the provider if vomiting occurs, and reassess the symptoms.","C":"Withhold digoxin, continue cardiac monitoring, notify the provider, and obtain serum digoxin, electrolytes, and renal function.","D":"Hold digoxin until potassium is corrected, continue cardiac monitoring, notify the provider, and resume the dose if the ectopy resolves."}}
saved_record.rationale: The combination of nausea, anorexia, fatigue, and new premature ventricular contractions is consistent with digoxin toxicity. The current digoxin label identifies hypokalemia as a factor that predisposes to toxicity and directs clinicians to obtain a serum digoxin level when toxicity is suspected, assess electrolytes and renal function, interrupt or discontinue digoxin as appropriate, and use cardiac monitoring. A potassium value of 3.1 mmol/L is below the Mayo Clinic Laboratories adult reference interval of 3.6–5.2 mmol/L. Therefore C is the best answer. A and B give another digoxin dose despite a toxicity pattern. D incorrectly treats correction of potassium and improvement in ectopy as sufficient grounds to resume digoxin without completing the toxicity evaluation.
saved_record.source_claim_supported: Digoxin toxicity can present with anorexia, nausea, fatigue and ventricular premature contractions; hypokalemia predisposes to toxicity. When toxicity is suspected, obtain serum digoxin data, assess electrolytes and renal function, interrupt/discontinue digoxin as appropriate, and use cardiac monitoring.
